3	**Question:** How is the code organized, built, and kept honest?  
4	**Artifacts:** this document, [`testing.md`](testing.md) (the testing half of this
5	view), `CLAUDE.md` (the short form an agent always has loaded)  
6	**Notation:** Markdown  
7	**For the agent:** the most important view, and the one to read **before writing
8	anything** in `src/main/java/`. Every rule here saves a correction in every use
9	case.
10	
11	Most of what follows is **enforced executably** by
12	`src/test/java/ai/unifiedprocess/petclinic/ArchitectureTest.java` (ArchUnit, runs
13	with `./mvnw test`). Each rule names the section it comes from, so a failure

15	rule in the same commit — a rule that contradicts this document is the rule

1	# Business Rules
2	
3	Rules that more than one use case must honour.
4	
5	A rule that belongs to a single use case stays **in** that use case as
6	`BR-NNN` — it is part of that use case's story and has no life of its own. A
7	rule that several use cases share lives **here** as `GR-NNN`, is stated once,
8	and is referenced by each use case that applies it. The use case keeps its local
9	`BR-NNN` heading, so tests and the traceability sensors still point at a rule of
10	that use case; the heading says which shared rule it realizes instead of
11	restating it.
12	
13	`BusinessRuleTraceabilityTest` (`./mvnw test`) keeps the two sides honest: it
14	fails when a use case references a rule that does not exist, when a link lands
15	on a renamed heading, when the `**Realized by:**` line and the use cases
16	disagree in either direction, when the summary table drifts from the rules below
17	it, or when a rule here is realized by fewer than two use cases.
18	
19	**Why `GR` and not `BR`.** `BR-NNN` ids are scoped to a use case: every
20	`UC-NNN-*.md` numbers its rules from `BR-001`, and `@UseCase(businessRules =
21	"BR-001")` is resolved inside that one file. A global `BR-001` would therefore
22	stand beside ten local ones and mean nothing on its own. `GR` — global rule —
23	is a second namespace precisely so that an id never needs a use case to
24	disambiguate it.

46

trajectory.message:
UC-002 is implemented and `./mvnw -q test` passes. I didn't run `./mvnw verify`, so there's no Playwright test for it and no merged coverage report.

- **Repository:** `VetRepository` (in `vet/domain`) has `findPage(offset, limit)` and `count()`. It loads each vet's specialties in the same query, sorted alphabetically (BR-002). Vets are ordered by last name, first name, then id.
- **View:** `VetsView` at `/vets` shows a lazily loaded grid with First Name, Last Name and Specialties. The Specialties column shows "none" when a vet has none, and an empty clinic shows an empty grid. It needs no login (BR-003). I set the chunk size to 50, since the spec doesn't give one.
- **Navigation:** `MainLayout` now links to `VetsView.class` instead of the string `"vets"`.
- **Tests:** `UC002ViewVeterinariansTest` has three tests:
  - **Main flow:** it checks the ordering and the specialty text for the seeded vets, and that the "Veterinarians" nav item points at `/vets`. Clicking the nav item doesn't navigate in browserless tests, so the test navigates to `VetsView` directly.
  - **Lazy loading:** it adds 100 vets and checks the grid reports 106 rows and that the last one loads on demand.
  - **A1 (empty clinic):** it deletes all vets and checks the grid is empty.

I did not change the `Status:` line in the use case, since the project requires a `coverage-check` audit first.
